q: Which electricity emission factor should an Indian exporter use for CBAM indirect emissions?
title: Electricity factor for CBAM in India
short: For cement and fertilisers, indirect emissions count, and the default electricity factor for India comes from the EU implementing act on CBAM default values, not from the CEA. A lower actual factor needs a direct technical link to a generator or a power purchase agreement that meets the CBAM conditions, with evidence.

ul: Default factor for India, set in the EU implementing act on default values (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2621, corrected by 2026/1740).
Actual factor from a captive or directly linked plant, backed by metering and fuel records.
Actual factor under a power purchase agreement that meets the CBAM conditions.

p: Indirect emissions are not part of the charged figure for iron, steel, aluminium or hydrogen, so this choice matters mainly for cement and fertilisers.
Monthly units by source, power purchase agreements and metering records, and a note of which factor you used and why. Renewable certificates do not lower the factor.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel, electricity and production documents into dated, fingerprinted installation records, the starting point for the actual emissions an EU importer asks for.
